text:
Tom Wilson's week was about a hit. He was ejected for boarding Florida's Sandis Vilmanis on Nov. 7 after only 2:12 of ice time, Vilmanis left the game, and the Department of Player Safety chose not to suspend him. Florida Hockey Now's headline spoke for the Panthers: "No Suspension for Tom Wilson after Hit on Sandis Vilmanis. That's Wrong." His explanation, as RMNB carried it: "I was trying to make a north-south hit."

On the ice, the drought is the story. He has no goals in 13 games on 3.9 expected goals, and two goals all season on 5.5 expected, after scoring 30 last season. The process holds: his individual expected goals per 60 (1.09) is exactly last season's rate, and Washington takes 55% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on. The finishing is what has gone missing.

His ice time is down about two minutes a night over his last ten, which is worth watching. Evolving-Hockey had him among the league's best two-way forwards last season (99th percentile at suppressing chances). Our numbers say the goals should come if the looks keep coming.
headline: Tom Wilson's drought, and the hit that overshadowed it
